newsitem.title: USA: S.F Fed to complete mortgage report in April - Parry.
newsitem.headline: S.F Fed to complete mortgage report in April - Parry.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco expects to complete by late April a project aimed at determining whether minority residents faced discriminatory treatment when applying for mortgage loans in the area, bank president Robert Parry said.
The project, launched in May 1996, followed a similar program initially conducted by the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland.
Reserve Banks in Boston, New York, Chicago and St. Louis also adopted similar efforts at the same time as the San Francisco Fed.

"By April 30 of this year, all five Reserve Banks will have completed their local projects and compiled the results into a series of final reports," Parry said at a conference of the Mortgage Credit Partnership (MCP) program.
Parry praised the program, adding that "in addition to the subtlety with which discrimination may occur, several other factors made San Francisco a challenging city in which to conduct this project."
Parry said affordability was also a major problem concerning residents planning to purchase a home. "The reality is many residents can't afford to purchase a home here," the Fed president said.
